n: Given on a Sabbath in Missouri, the day Polly Knight was buried, this revelation blesses those who came to Zion with pure motives and obedience.

f.w: an eye single to my glory

n: Those who live will inherit the earth; those who die will rest, their works following them, and receive a crown in the Father’s mansions. Polly Knight had prayed to see Zion before she died.

f.w: their works shall follow them
the mansions of my Father

n: Those standing in Zion who obey the gospel will receive earth’s good things as it yields in full strength.
The faithful will also receive heavenly blessings, many commandments, and revelations in due time. More commandments are counted as a blessing, not a burden.

f.w: commandments not a few

n: The first great commandment: love God with all your heart, might, mind, and strength, and serve him in Jesus Christ’s name.

f.w: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God

n: The second: love your neighbor as yourself. Don’t steal, commit adultery, kill, or do anything like it—the spirit, not just the letter, of the law.

f.w: Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself
nor do anything like unto it
f.g: Avoid not only the act but anything resembling it.

n: Thank God in all things—even trials.

f.w: thank the Lord thy God in all things

n: The sacrifice God wants is a broken heart and contrite spirit, which replaced animal sacrifices after Christ.

f.w: a broken heart and a contrite spirit

n: To stay unspotted from the world, go to the house of prayer and offer your sacraments on the Lord’s holy day. This is a key Sabbath scripture.

f.w: unspotted from the world
my holy day

n: The Sabbath is appointed for rest from labor and devotion to God.

f.w: to pay thy devotions unto the Most High
f.g: To worship and give reverent attention to God.

n: Yet righteous devotion and vows to God belong to every day, not only Sunday.

f.w: vows
f.g: Sacred promises or offerings to God.

n: On the Lord’s day especially, offer your oblations—offerings—and sacraments, and confess sins to fellow Saints and to the Lord.

f.w: oblations
f.g: Offerings to God of time, talents, or means.

n: Do no other work that day; prepare food with singleness of heart so your fasting may be perfect—or, in other words, your joy full.

f.w: singleness of heart

n: The Lord explains that fasting and prayer are, in essence, rejoicing and prayer. True Sabbath observance is joyful.
Do these things with thanksgiving and cheerful faces—but not with excessive, frivolous laughter. A glad heart is different from shallow levity.

f.w: not with much laughter

n: Do this and the fulness of the earth is yours: animals, birds, and creatures that climb and walk.

f.w: the fulness of the earth is yours

n: Plants and earth’s good things—for food, clothing, houses, barns, orchards, gardens, and vineyards—are yours too.

f.w: herb

n: Everything from the earth in its season is made for human use—both to please the eye and to gladden the heart. God created beauty, not just utility.

f.w: both to please the eye and to gladden the heart

n: For food, clothing, taste, and smell; to strengthen the body and enliven the soul.
God is pleased to give these gifts, but they must be used wisely—not to excess and not by extortion.

f.w: with judgment, not to excess, neither by extortion
f.g: With good sense, in moderation, and without exploiting others.

n: Nothing offends God more than failing to acknowledge his hand in all things and disobeying his commandments. Gratitude is central.

f.w: confess not his hand in all things

n: This is consistent with the law and the prophets; the Lord asks the Saints not to trouble him further about it.

f.w: the law and the prophets

n: Those who do righteous works will receive peace in this world and eternal life in the next—a well-loved promise.

f.w: peace in this world, and eternal life in the world to come

n: The Lord has spoken, and the Spirit testifies of it.
